question: 'Midnight's Children' which portrays India's transition from British colonial rule to independence and partition of India is written by :
solution:
The correct answer is __**Salman Rushdie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Midnight's Children' **

 
 
• The book Midnight's Children was written by **Salman Rushdie in 1981**.
 
• **Bill Botten **created the cover for the book's **publication by Jonathan Cape**.
 
• It depicts the **evolution of India from British colonial authority to independence and division**.
 
• It is regarded as a prime example of **postmodern, magical realist, and postcolonial literature**. 
 
• **Saleem Sinai**, who serves as the narrative's main protagonist, tells the tale, which is based on** real historical occurrences**.
 
• Fictional reports are written in a **self-reflexive** manner to preserve history.
 
• In 1981, Midnight's Children earned both the **James Tait Black Memorial Prize and the Booker Prize**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other achievements**

 
 
• To celebrate the **Booker Prize's 25th and 40th anniversaries**, it was given the **"Booker of Bookers" Prize** and the best-ever prize winners in **1993 and 2008**.
 
• The book was included in the **BBC's The Big Read survey of the UK's "best-loved novels" in 2003**.
 
• The **Penguin Books publication's**, list of the Great Books of the 20th Century also included it.
 
• The book was chosen as one of the** 70 titles in the Big Jubilee Read in 2022**, a celebration of Commonwealth writers' writing for the **Platinum Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II**.
